subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: At any point t on the curve x = a(t + sin t), y = a(1 − cos t), find the lengths of the tangent, the normal, the subtangent and the subnormal.

mark_split.label: Find the slope and write y in half-angle form
State the four formulas and find √(1 + m²)
Find the subtangent and the subnormal
Find the lengths of the tangent and the normal

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what the slope comes to, name the four formulas you use, and say which half-angle identities you need.

steps.label: Find the slope and write y in half-angle form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two half-angle identities do all the simplifying here: 1 + cos t = 2cos²(t/2), 1 − cos t = 2sin²(t/2) and sin t = 2 sin(t/2)cos(t/2). Convert both y and m before going any further.
lines: x = a(t + sin t)  ⇒  dx/dt = a(1 + cos t) = 2a cos²(t/2)
y = a(1 − cos t)  ⇒  dy/dt = a sin t = 2a sin(t/2)cos(t/2)
Also  y = a(1 − cos t) = 2a sin²(t/2)
Take 0 < t < π, so sin(t/2) > 0 and cos(t/2) > 0 and every length below is positive.

recall.must_convey: That m = dy/dt over dx/dt = tan(t/2), and that y = 2a sin²(t/2).
accept: differentiate x and y with respect to t and divide
the slope comes to tan of t by two
one plus cos t is two cos squared t by two
half angle formulas use chesi tan t by two ki teesukovali
y equals two a sin squared t by two
dy by dt over dx by dt gives the slope

steps.why: The four quantities all contain y and m, so simplifying both into half-angle form once at the start means the rest of the work is short cancelling instead of long trigonometry.
common_mistakes: Writing dx/dt as a(1 − cos t) by copying the y-derivative pattern.
Using 1 + cos t = 2sin²(t/2), which is the identity for 1 − cos t.
Leaving m as sin t/(1 + cos t) and then being unable to simplify sec and tan later.
steps.memory_tip: Minus goes with sine and plus goes with cosine: 1 − cos t = 2sin²(t/2), 1 + cos t = 2cos²(t/2).

steps.label: State the four formulas and find √(1 + m²)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The four definitions are worth a mark on their own. 1 + tan²(t/2) = sec²(t/2) is the identity that makes the two lengths simplify.
lines: At a point where the slope is m,
length of tangent = |y√(1 + m²)/m|,   length of normal = |y√(1 + m²)|

recall.must_convey: That the four formulas are y/m, ym, |y√(1+m²)/m| and |y√(1+m²)|, and that √(1 + m²) = sec(t/2).
accept: subtangent is y by m and subnormal is y into m
length of tangent is y root one plus m squared by m
length of normal is y root one plus m squared
naalugu formulas rasi root one plus m squared ni sec t by two ga marchali
one plus tan squared is sec squared
state all four definitions before substituting

steps.why: Students most often lose marks here by mixing up subtangent and subnormal. Writing all four definitions down first, before any substitution, makes the mix-up impossible and earns the mark by itself.
common_mistakes: Swapping subtangent and subnormal, so y/m and ym are used the wrong way round.
Answering only two of the four quantities the question asks for.
steps.memory_tip: Sub-TANGENT goes with the tangent, so m goes underneath as it does in the tangent line; sub-NORMAL goes with the normal, so m multiplies.

steps.label: Find the subtangent and the subnormal
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The subtangent simplifies all the way back to a sin t, which is a useful check: it is exactly dy/dt divided by a.
lines: which may also be written as a(1 − cos t)tan(t/2).

recall.must_convey: That the subtangent is a sin t and the subnormal is 2a sin³(t/2)/cos(t/2).
accept: subtangent is y by m which simplifies to a sin t
subnormal is y into m which is two a sin cubed t by two over cos t by two
divide two a sin squared by tan t by two
subtangent a sin t vasthundi and subnormal lo tan undipotundi
the subnormal can also be written as a into one minus cos t into tan t by two
two sin t by two cos t by two is sin t

steps.why: Dividing by tan(t/2) is the same as multiplying by cos(t/2)/sin(t/2), which cancels one sine and leaves the double-angle form 2 sin(t/2)cos(t/2) = sin t. Doing the division as a fraction of fractions is where the cancelling is usually missed.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by tan(t/2) for the subtangent instead of dividing.
Leaving the subtangent as 2a sin²(t/2)/tan(t/2) without simplifying to a sin t.
Writing 2 sin(t/2)cos(t/2) as sin(t/2) rather than sin t.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing by a tangent flips it to cos over sin, and one sine always cancels.

steps.label: Find the lengths of the tangent and the normal
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The length of the tangent comes to 2a sin(t/2), which equals √(2ay) — a quick check, since y = 2a sin²(t/2). Present all four answers together in the box.

lines.text: ∴ length of tangent = 2a sin(t/2),  length of normal = 2a sin(t/2)tan(t/2),  subtangent = a sin t,  subnormal = 2a sin³(t/2)/cos(t/2)

recall.must_convey: That the length of the tangent is 2a sin(t/2) and the length of the normal is 2a sin(t/2)tan(t/2), and that all four answers are given.
accept: length of tangent is two a sin t by two
length of normal is two a sin t by two into tan t by two
multiply y by sec t by two and divide by tan t by two
naalugu answers ni kalipi rayali
sec by tan simplifies to cos by sin times one by cos
the length of the tangent squared is two a y
heard_as: two a sin t by two

steps.why: The question names four quantities, so all four must appear in the final answer. A script that gives two of them is a half answer and is marked as one.
common_mistakes: Giving only the subtangent and the subnormal and stopping there.
Cancelling sec(t/2) against tan(t/2) incorrectly and losing the factor sin(t/2).
Writing the length of the normal as 2a sin²(t/2), forgetting the sec(t/2) factor.
steps.memory_tip: The two lengths differ by one factor of m: length of normal = m × length of tangent, exactly as subnormal = m² × subtangent.

insider_note: Half-angle forms turn both derivatives into neat products, giving m = tan(t/2). All four lengths then follow from y and m, so get those two right before anything else.
